headline: Cricketer Nayeem Hasan assaulted by police in CNG, claims 'mental devastation'
summary: The BCB medical team has arrived in Chattogram to assess the physical condition of the cricketer after he alleged police harassment.
details: Cricketer Nayeem Hasan has alleged that he was assaulted by police officers while inside a CNG auto-rickshaw. He claims that officers grabbed his throat and that he is now mentally devastated by the experience.
Nayeem further alleged that upon arriving at the police station, the Officer-in-Charge (OC) told him to 'speak with eyes lowered,' implying a disrespectful treatment of the authority.
In response to the incident, the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) has sent a medical team to Chattogram to evaluate the physical state of the athlete.
The Commissioner of the Chattogram Metropolitan Police (CMP) has vowed that maximum action will be taken against those involved in the harassment of the athlete.
The CMP Commissioner stated that no one will be spared if found guilty of the assault, promising a strict investigation into the matter.
caption:
“Police grabbed my throat after putting me in a CNG; I am mentally devastated.”

Cricketer Nayeem Hasan has alleged that he was assaulted by police officers while inside a CNG auto-rickshaw. He claims that officers grabbed his throat and that he is now mentally devastated by the experience.

Nayeem further alleged that upon arriving at the police station, the Officer-in-Charge (OC) told him to 'speak with eyes lowered,' implying a disrespectful treatment of the authority.

In response to the incident, the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) has sent a medical team to Chattogram to evaluate the physical state of the athlete.

The Commissioner of the Chattogram Metropolitan Police (CMP) has vowed that maximum action will be taken against those involved in the harassment of the athlete.

The CMP Commissioner stated that no one will be spared if found guilty of the assault, promising a strict investigation into the matter.

headline: Trump says deal to end war with Iran to be signed Sunday
summary: US President Donald Trump and Pakistan claim a peace framework is ready, but Iran denies a signing will take place this Sunday.
details: US President Donald Trump and mediator Pakistan announced on Saturday that an initial deal to end the war in West Asia would be signed on Sunday. Pakistani PM Shehbaz Sharif stated that both sides agreed on a framework, preparing for an electronic signing.

Trump posted on social media that the deal would immediately open the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global oil artery that Iran has blocked. However, Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei cautioned that the signing will not happen tomorrow, citing hesitation from the other side.

The proposed memorandum of understanding involves reopening the strait and lifting the US naval blockade. In exchange, the US would begin releasing billions of dollars in frozen Iranian assets and waive sanctions on oil exports.

A critical point of contention remains Iran's nuclear programme. While a US official stated the deal would lead to the dismantling of the programme, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi indicated Iran wants to retain uranium in diluted form.

The conflict, which began on February 28 with joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran, has killed thousands of people, mostly in Iran and Lebanon. Global energy prices have spiked as a result of the ongoing hostilities.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has stated that Israel will not be party to the agreement, clashing with Trump over demands to curb military action in Lebanon.
caption:
A peace deal to end the West Asia war is reportedly imminent, but the US and Iran are contradicting each other on the timing.

US President Donald Trump and mediator Pakistan announced on Saturday that an initial deal to end the war in West Asia would be signed on Sunday. Pakistani PM Shehbaz Sharif stated that both sides agreed on a framework, preparing for an electronic signing.

Trump posted on social media that the deal would immediately open the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global oil artery that Iran has blocked. However, Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei cautioned that the signing will not happen tomorrow, citing hesitation from the other side.

The proposed memorandum of understanding involves reopening the strait and lifting the US naval blockade. In exchange, the US would begin releasing billions of dollars in frozen Iranian assets and waive sanctions on oil exports.

A critical point of contention remains Iran's nuclear programme. While a US official stated the deal would lead to the dismantling of the programme, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi indicated Iran wants to retain uranium in diluted form.

The conflict, which began on February 28 with joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran, has killed thousands of people, mostly in Iran and Lebanon. Global energy prices have spiked as a result of the ongoing hostilities.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has stated that Israel will not be party to the agreement, clashing with Trump over demands to curb military action in Lebanon.
